# the contributor independent audit: arbitrary simplex containers

Read `candidate 159eef4ea58ca5da`
in full. Verdict PASS, no correction needed. The independent exact
verifier was rerun and passed16332 checks, including978 arbitrary
orientation small-area cases. This is an auxiliary obstruction, not
an OC counterexample.

The source has exactly three actual full-dimensional fibers: its
middle triangle contains the endpoint Minkowski midpoint, and grouping
base coefficients proves the claimed fiber identities. Projection is
[0,2], so every induced integer base is accounted for. Only the truncated
triangle endpoint has a nonzero ordinary depth deficit, and its explicit
containing-simplex cap cover gives the stated O(epsilon^2) upper bound
for the maximum over every candidate.

The nested-triangle lemma has no orientation restriction. Exterior
pyramids over the three long edges of the truncated triangle give
uniform bounds on every point of an arbitrary enclosing triangle.
The minimum-sum, maximum-x, and maximum-y vertices are distinct and
therefore list all vertices. Their coordinate estimates give a strictly
positive orientation determinant. The two oriented-edge inequalities
at (epsilon,0) and (0,epsilon) are correct, including their positive
denominators and the subsequent one-sided absolute-value estimates.
They force the minimum-sum vertex below the middle body's retained
facet by at least epsilon/2. The resulting exterior pyramid contributes
at least31epsilon/256 after middle-fiber rescaling, unless the endpoint
already has the required epsilon/16 added area.

For arbitrary triangle choices the actual middle convexified fiber need
not be a triangle. The proof correctly uses only that its double is
convex and contains both the original middle triangle and the first
container: the last endpoint container contains0. Thus the nested
lemma applies to every choice, whether separately minimizing or jointly
optimized. All other added areas are nonnegative. Binary layers remain
separate at their integer extremes, so the extension to more integer
variables is valid.

The final contradiction compares the positive lower bound with the
upper bound on summed deficits and does not divide by an unproved
positive denominator. It leaves the complete OC claim untouched.

## Audit of the no-heavy-fiber extension

Section 5 subsequently read in full. The exposed binary layer argument
preserves all three lower fibers and all three added upper triangle
fibers exactly. The total area expansion is correct, and W>79/32 with
each fiber at most 1/2 gives the stated uniform strict margin below W/4.
For arbitrary choices of all six enclosing triangles the exposed lower
layer retains the earlier epsilon/16 obstruction. Upper-layer excess is
nonnegative. Binary padding multiplies both deficit and added area while
leaving each individual fiber area unchanged. Thus the obstruction also
holds outside the heavy-fiber regime for every n>=2. The complete updated
verifier was rerun: PASS 16332 rational checks and 520 layer/padding checks.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
